_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Cameroon covering Bantu origins and migrations, Sao civilisation, Kanem-Bornu and Fulani influences, German Kamerun, French/British mandate split, Ahidjo and Biya presidencies, Anglophone crisis, and Boko Haram spillover.

ethnic_groups.name: Bamileke/Bamoun
ethnic_groups.notes: Western highlands; Bamileke chiefdoms with elaborate masquerade traditions; Bamoun Sultanate with Njoya's script

ethnic_groups.name: Beti-Pahuin (Ewondo, Bulu, Fang)
ethnic_groups.notes: South and Centre regions; includes Ewondo around Yaoundé; Beti languages

ethnic_groups.name: Bassa/Bakoko
ethnic_groups.notes: Littoral and Centre regions; early nationalist role

ethnic_groups.name: Fulani/Peul
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Cameroon; pastoral and urban Muslim communities; lamidates under Adamawa Emirate heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Duala
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal people; historical trading intermediaries; city of Douala named after them

ethnic_groups.name: Kirdi/Mafa
ethnic_groups.notes: Non-Muslim highland peoples of the Mandara Mountains; includes Mafa, Mofu, Kapsiki; resist Fulani expansion

ethnic_groups.name: Baka (Pygmy)
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern rainforest hunter-gatherers; threatened by logging and displacement

ethnic_groups.name: Anglophone Groups (Meta, Nso, Bakweri)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northwest and Southwest regions; English-speaking minority driving Anglophone crisis

independence.from: France (French Cameroun); 1961 reunification with British Southern Cameroons

natural_resources.notes: Oil production declining (from peak 1985); timber second export (tropical hardwoods, deforestation concern); enormous hydropower potential (Lom Pangar, Nachtigal); iron ore deposits at Mbalam (undeveloped, Chinese interest); 'Africa in miniature' agricultural diversity

military.notes: Fighting Boko Haram in Far North; Anglophone crisis in Northwest/Southwest (separatist conflict since 2017, 'Ambazonia'); Rapid Intervention Battalion (BIR) elite force; French military base in Douala; Multinational Joint Task Force against Boko Haram

natural_hazards: volcanic activity (Mount Cameroon, Africa's most active volcano)
Lake Nyos-type limnic eruptions (1986 disaster killed 1,746)

debt_aid.notes: HIPC debt relief beneficiary; Chinese infrastructure loans significant; IMF Extended Credit Facility; dual English/French administration increases costs

education.notes: Bilingual system (French/English) mirrors colonial dual mandate; Anglophone regions feel marginalized in education policy; Boko Haram and Anglophone conflict closing schools in north/west; GCE/Baccalauréat dual system

diaspora_migration.notes: Hosts CAR/Nigerian refugees; Anglophone crisis produced 60k+ refugees (Nigeria) and 600k+ IDPs; brain drain of Anglophone professionals significant; Cameroon passport among weakest globally

digital_economy.notes: Silicon Mountain (Buea) was thriving Anglophone tech hub before conflict disrupted it; mobile money adoption high; internet shutdowns in Anglophone regions (2017-ongoing, world's longest); Kiro'o Games (African gaming studio)

current_leader.name: Paul Biya
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: One of Africa's longest-serving leaders; in power 40+ years; CPDM party

former_leaders.name: Ahmadou Ahidjo
former_leaders.notes: First president; northern Fulani; centralised state; resigned and went into exile; died in Senegal 1989

910.name: Bantu Origins and Early Peoples of Cameroon
910.description: The Cameroon-Nigeria borderland is the probable Bantu homeland; early ironworking and agricultural communities spread across the region.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Cradle and Proto-Bantu Dispersal
sub_clusters.description: Linguistic and archaeological evidence places the proto-Bantu homeland in the Cameroon Grassfields; initial southward and eastward migrations begin.

sub_clusters.name: Early Ironworking and Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Iron smelting develops in the Mandara Mountains and Grassfields; yam and oil-palm cultivation supports population growth.

910.name: Sao Civilisation of the Lake Chad Basin
910.description: The Sao people build fortified settlements in the Logone-Chari floodplain; terracotta figurines and bronze-working flourish.

sub_clusters.name: Sao Walled Settlements
sub_clusters.description: Sao mound settlements along the Logone and Chari rivers; distinctive terracotta sculpture tradition; fishing and agriculture.

sub_clusters.name: Sao Decline and Kotoko Succession
sub_clusters.description: Kanem-Bornu expansion absorbs Sao communities; Kotoko city-states emerge as successors in the far north.

920.name: Kanem-Bornu Influence in Northern Cameroon
920.description: The Kanem-Bornu Empire extends suzerainty over Mandara, Kotoko, and other northern Cameroon polities; Islam spreads via trade and conquest.

sub_clusters.name: Mandara Sultanate
sub_clusters.description: Mandara kingdom in the Mandara Mountains converts to Islam; mediates between Bornu and southern highland peoples.

sub_clusters.name: Trans-Saharan and Trans-Sudanic Trade
sub_clusters.description: Slave, ivory, and cloth trade links northern Cameroon to Bornu, Tripoli, and the Hausa states.

920.name: Grassfields Kingdoms and Bamoun Sultanate
920.description: Tikar-related chiefdoms and the Bamoun Sultanate develop centralised kingdoms in the western highlands; artistic traditions flourish.

sub_clusters.name: Bamoun Sultanate and King Njoya
sub_clusters.description: The Bamoun Sultanate under Sultan Njoya develops a unique script (Shu Mom), converts to Islam, and creates an elaborate court culture.

sub_clusters.name: Bamileke and Tikar Chiefdoms
sub_clusters.description: Decentralised but hierarchical Bamileke chiefdoms in the western highlands; elaborate secret societies and masquerade traditions.

930.name: Fulani Jihad and Adamawa Emirate
930.description: Modibbo Adama leads Fulani jihad into northern Cameroon as part of the Sokoto Caliphate; Adamawa Emirate transforms the region.

sub_clusters.name: Founding of the Adamawa Emirate
sub_clusters.description: Modibbo Adama receives a flag from Usman dan Fodio; establishes Yola as capital; subordinate lamidates across northern Cameroon.

sub_clusters.name: Fulani Slave Raiding and Resistance
sub_clusters.description: Fulani lamidates raid non-Muslim 'kirdi' peoples of the Mandara Mountains and Adamawa Plateau; fierce resistance from Gbaya and other groups.

940.name: German Kamerun (1884–1916)
940.description: Germany establishes Kamerun protectorate; plantation economy on the coast; expansion into interior; World War I campaigns end German rule.

sub_clusters.name: German Annexation and Gustav Nachtigal
sub_clusters.description: Gustav Nachtigal signs treaties with Douala chiefs; Kamerun protectorate proclaimed at Scramble for Africa; coastal plantation economy (cocoa, rubber, palm oil).

sub_clusters.name: German Conquest of the Interior
sub_clusters.description: Military expeditions subdue Adamawa, Bamoun, and Bamileke areas; forced labour for railways and plantations; Neukamerun acquired from France 1911.

sub_clusters.name: World War I Kamerun Campaign
sub_clusters.description: Allied (British, French, Belgian) forces invade; Germans resist until Mora garrison surrenders February 1916; colony partitioned.

940.name: French and British Mandates (1916–1960)
940.description: League of Nations mandates divide Cameroon; French Cameroun (80%) and British Cameroons develop under different colonial systems.

sub_clusters.name: French Cameroun Mandate and Trusteeship
sub_clusters.description: Indigénat system; forced labour for infrastructure; UPC nationalist movement; brutal suppression of Bamileke insurrection (1955–1960).

sub_clusters.name: British Cameroons and the Plebiscite
sub_clusters.description: British Cameroons administered as part of Nigeria; 1961 plebiscite: Northern Cameroons joins Nigeria, Southern Cameroons joins Cameroun Republic.

950.name: Ahmadou Ahidjo and Nation-Building
950.description: Ahidjo leads independent Cameroon; federal then unitary state; one-party CNU rule; suppression of UPC insurgency; oil economy begins.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Reunification
sub_clusters.description: French Cameroun independent 1 January 1960; Southern Cameroons reunification creates Federal Republic 1 October 1961.

sub_clusters.name: Ahidjo's Unitary One-Party State
sub_clusters.description: Federation abolished 1972 (United Republic); single-party CNU regime; political centralisation; Ahidjo resigns 1982, hands power to Biya.

960.name: Paul Biya Era (1982–Present)
960.description: Biya becomes one of Africa's longest-ruling leaders; multiparty transition; economic crisis; Anglophone crisis escalates to armed conflict; Boko Haram spillover in the Far North.

sub_clusters.name: Biya's Consolidation of Power
sub_clusters.description: Failed 1984 coup; Ahidjo exiled; CPDM replaces CNU; austerity under structural adjustment; democratic opening under pressure.

sub_clusters.name: Multiparty Politics and Ghost Towns
sub_clusters.description: Villes mortes (ghost town) campaign; opposition leader John Fru Ndi; contested elections; oil revenues sustain patronage networks.

sub_clusters.name: Anglophone Crisis and Armed Conflict
sub_clusters.description: Lawyers' and teachers' strikes escalate; Ambazonia separatist declaration; military crackdown; humanitarian crisis displacing hundreds of thousands.

sub_clusters.name: Boko Haram in the Far North
sub_clusters.description: Boko Haram and ISWAP attacks spill from Nigeria into Cameroon's Far North; multinational joint task force; civilian displacement.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
